verdict_text: Prototype methodology is implementable, but synchronization and frame quality are not yet sufficient to authorize corpus regeneration.

alignment_method.clock: bounded 0.1 s grid cross-correlation of norm(phone accelerometer - phone gravity) against norm(vehicle indicated longitudinal/lateral acceleration)
alignment_method.rotation: gravity-anchored proper rotation solved by weighted Kabsch using phone gravity and vehicle longitudinal/lateral acceleration vectors
target_independent_signals: vehicle yaw rate retained for validation

coordinate_conventions.phone: source Android sensor axes; Variant A gyro names are retained as yaw/pitch/roll but their physical axis mapping remains a limitation
coordinate_conventions.gravity: positive +g source gravity vector constrains vehicle +Up

label_qa_policy: performed after alignment parameter estimation only; target retained unless independently disproven
limitations: source clocks exhibit resets and large duration differences; a constant offset is not universally adequate
dynamic acceleration Kabsch is weak on straight/low-dynamics segments and cannot prove frame correctness alone
Variant A gyro yaw/pitch/roll semantics require source-level confirmation
wheel speed cannot be converted without wheel-radius/odometry calibration
this prototype does not regenerate data

regeneration_gate.indicated_speed_independently_consistent: requires review of reported QA metrics
regeneration_gate.recommendation: NO-GO until rejected/reset segments are handled and transform/synchronization quality thresholds are reviewed on train/validation

proposed_deterministic_algorithm: estimate target-independent clock offset per overlapping segment
reject insufficient overlap or excessive drift
estimate gravity-anchored rotation from dynamic acceleration references
compare indicated speed with vehicle GPS velocity as QA
fit normalization on train trips only
